title: Tianji Trial
next_chapter_hook: The words from that eye pierced his heart like an ice pick—'Your pretended death was merely a performance I permitted.' Chen Ji's chessboard of fate is being quietly manipulated from above.

text.content: The moment the token entered his hand, a warmth surged from his palm straight to his celestial spirit. Chen Ji lowered his gaze to study it—the patterns corresponded one-to-one with the runes on the Turtle Shell artifact, curvature, spacing, and spiritual resonance matching perfectly. His thumb gently traced the engravings, and his fingertip received a fine prickling sensation, as if countless needles were wriggling beneath his skin. 'The layout of the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion extends far deeper than I ever imagined.' He silently chanted in his heart, yet a cold glint flickered across his eyes. On the token's reverse was carved a small character 'Trial', its brushwork ancient and unadorned, with a faint golden light faintly flowing within.

He stepped through the entrance of the ruins. The blue stone corridor sealed shut behind him with a thunderous roar, completely cutting off the last trace of daylight. In the darkness, the token self-illuminated with a ghostly blue glow, illuminating a staircase extending forward. Strangely—this staircase did not go downward, but slanted upward, as if leading to some dimension that did not exist in the real world. Chen Ji's steps did not pause, silently counting in his heart: one step, two steps, three steps... When the seventh step landed, the sensation beneath his foot suddenly vanished.

He did not fall. The stone steps transformed into flowing light, gently cradling him as it rose into an endless void. Before his eyes there was no sky, no earth—only endless nebula vortices slowly rotating around him. In the distance stood a massive white jade altar, upon which burned three perpetual lanterns, their flames colored black, white, and gray respectively. 'Trial space.' Chen Ji steadied himself, his gaze sweeping across the surroundings, 'The internal rules are completely different from the outside world—here, the consumption of Heavenly Fate will be ten times that of the outside.' He sensed that thin strand of Heavenly Fate within him, slowly dissipating at a visible rate.

At the center of the altar, a pitch-black coffin lay motionless. When Chen Ji approached, the inscriptions on the coffin lid actually self-manifested with blood-red light—'Chapter Seven Hundred, Death.' The four characters were like brands, deeply embedded in the center of the coffin lid. He had known this prophecy long ago, but seeing it presented in such a concrete manner still caused his heart to skip an involuntary beat. This coffin contained his ending.

At this moment, a massive eye abruptly opened in the void. The pupil was black as an abyss, the iris a burning gold, and within the vertical pupil countless scenes of stellar destruction and rebirth swirled. That eye spanned heaven and earth, taking the entire altar into its field of vision, regarding Chen Ji as one might regard a contemptible ant. 'You have arrived.' The voice sounded from all directions simultaneously, ancient and authoritative, yet carrying a suffocating indifference, 'The inheritor of the Tianji Record has finally stood before the origin of destiny.'

dialogue.content: 'You have seen your ending—Chapter Seven Hundred, annihilation.' That eye's vertical pupil slightly contracted, the golden iris rippling with mocking satisfaction, 'This is the will of heaven. The fragment in your hands is merely a glimpse through a tube, and I... am the sky above your head.' The voice rang like a great bell, making Chen Ji's eardrums ache, 'Now, make your choice.'

text.content: The white jade altar suddenly cracked open four fissures, and four massive stone tablets rose from the cracks, each inscribed with a distinctly different path. Chen Ji stood in place, his gaze scanning those inscriptions inch by inch, his mind racing. The Eye of Heavenly Dao had made its move—not a physical attack, but a judgment directly作用于 the level of destiny. He felt that eye scanning every inch of his soul, every heartbeat precisely recorded by it. 'It wants to see my choice.' A faint smile curved at the corner of his mouth, 'Very well, I will let you see.'

choice.prompt: The Eye of Heavenly Dao's voice reverberated through the void: 'Choose, holder of the Tianji Record. Your fate lies within your thoughts at this very moment.' Chen Ji drew a deep breath—his next step would determine the direction of this first clash with heaven.

choices.text: Submit passively and accept the prophecy
choices.description: Kneel before the coffin, acknowledging Chapter Seven Hundred's death as an established fact, trading dignity for time to breathe.
choices.visible_cost: Lose the will to resist against heaven
choices.risk_hint: Every favor heaven grants carries chains hidden beneath

text.content: Chen Ji slowly bent his knee, kneeling on one knee before the coffin. When his knee touched the cold jade surface, a chill spread through his entire body along his bones. 'I accept.' He hung his head, his voice low and submissive. A flicker of satisfaction crossed that eye's vertical pupil—the satisfaction a hunter feels when seeing prey bow its head. Chen Ji, head bowed,，嘴角却在无人能见的角度勾起一丝sneered：你要我跪，我就跪。你要看我低头，我就低头。但你休想看见我眼中有一丝真正的屈服。

choices.description: Walk to the coffin, point at that eye and demand: Who decreed that Chapter Seven Hundred must die?
choices.visible_cost: Provoke heaven and lose room for negotiation
choices.visible_reward: Force out more information from the Eye of Heavenly Dao
choices.risk_hint: A direct confrontation with heaven, the gap in strength is immense

text.content: 'Chapter Seven Hundred—who wrote it?' Chen Ji spoke each word with deliberate precision, stepping forward, his boot heel creating tangible ripples in the void. He tilted his head to直视那只金色的巨瞳，毫无惧色，'你说是天道意志，那我倒要问问——天道是谁？是你吗？'话音落下，虚空中炸开一道无形的雷鸣。陈机感到一股排山倒海的压力从四面八方挤压而来，他的骨骼在重压下发出咯吱之声。但他没有退，甚至没有皱眉。那只眼睛的竖瞳剧烈收缩了一瞬——它没有料到，一只蝼蚁竟敢直视它的imposing。

choices.description: Not rush to make a statement, first use the Tianji Record Fragment to deduce the true intentions behind these four stone tablets.
choices.visible_reward: Clearly see the trap nature behind the stone tablets
choices.risk_hint: The deduction process will be completely observed by Heavenly Dao

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes. His right hand quietly rested upon his chest—where the Tianji Record Fragment was faintly radiating heat. He did not speak, did not show any stance, instead pouring all his spirit into that incomplete prophetic power. The world before his eyes suddenly turned transparent: the four stone tablets stripped away their layered disguises in his vision—the first path led to eternal servitude, the second to being crushed to pieces, the third seemed safe but was actually an elaborately designed maze, and the fourth... deep within the fourth path, an eye lay hidden, watching. 'So that's how it is.' He opened his eyes, a knowing smile appearing at the corner of his mouth, 'You're testing me—testing what kind of person I am.'

choices.text: Refuse to participate in this game
choices.description: Turn away from the coffin and the giant eye, declaring himself unbound by these rules
choices.visible_cost: Be deemed heretical, inviting Heavenly Dao's full suppression
choices.visible_reward: Break the trial's narrative framework, making Heavenly Dao lose dominance for the first time
choices.risk_hint: Extremely dangerous, but the rewards are also the most abundant

text.content: Chen Ji turned around, his back facing the giant eye, and slowly walked toward the edge of the altar. 'I won't choose.' His voice was terrifyingly calm. 'You threaten me with death, seduce me with eternity, bait me with truth—but you forgot one thing.' He stopped, slightly tilting his head, revealing half of his stern profile, 'I am the holder of the Tianji Record. On fate's chessboard, I am not merely a piece—I am learning to be a Chess Player.' The golden vertical pupil violently trembled for an instant. In hundreds of millions of years, this was the first creature to dare speak the word 'no choice' before it.

The golden vertical pupil gazed at Chen Ji, its scrutinizing gaze gradually evolving into something more complex—a hunter's interest when discovering prey far more intriguing than anticipated. A low sigh echoed through the void, like an ancient giant beast turning over. 'Interesting.' The eye spoke, the coldness in its voice diminished, replaced by a chilling appreciation, 'In hundreds of millions of years, you are the first to say 'no choice' to me.'

The four stone tablets simultaneously trembled, dissolving into countless motes of light that remerged with the altar. The pitch-black coffin slowly sank beneath the white jade, as if everything just now had merely been an elaborately designed illusion. Chen Ji felt the oppressive weight suddenly lift, yet his nerves remained even tighter—the Heavenly Dao's eye had withdrawn, which absolutely did not mean it had lost, but rather that it had changed its strategy. 'What do you want to do?' he asked.

dialogue.content: 'I don't want to do anything.' The vertical pupil of that eye reflected Chen Ji's solitary figure standing on the altar, its lips seemingly curling into a derisive arc, 'I merely wish to remind you of something—you believe you're maneuvering the world, using the Tianji Record to peer into futures and calculate with precision. But have you ever considered... those 'futures' you窥见, who showed them to you?'

text.content: These words were like a basin of ice water poured over Chen Ji's head. His entire body froze, his complexion turning deathly pale in an instant. He recalled every activation of the Tianji Record Fragment—those visions, those prophecies, those conclusions he'd believed emerged from his meticulous calculations... how many had he truly 'seen' versus how many had been 'shown' to him? His fingers unconsciously clenched, knuckles whitening. This thought was too terrifying, causing the first crack in his rational defense that he'd always taken pride in.

dialogue.content: 'But you need not panic so quickly.' The eye's voice suddenly softened, the softness almost cruel, 'I offer you a chance—reveal the locations of the other six pages of the Tianji Record, and I'll help you alter the death prophecy in Chapter Seven Hundred. Then, you'll remain the infallible chess master, able to navigate the conflicts of the Three Great Sects with ease, and retrieve your sister.'

choice.prompt: The Heavenly Dao's eye made its offer: trading the locations of the Tianji Record Fragment for rewriting the death prophecy. Chen Ji had to make this choice in the blink of an eye—this was a true 'yang scheme.' Accepting meant surrendering his final trump card; refusing could invite immediate total annihilation from Heavenly Dao.

choices.text: Pretend to agree, secretly marking this debt
choices.description: First feign acceptance of the deal to buy survival space, later seek ways to counter it.
choices.visible_cost: Must disclose the location of one page of the Tianji Record
choices.visible_reward: Gain breathing room and Heavenly Dao's lowered guard
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Dao can peer into hearts; disguise may not be effective

text.content: 'Deal.' Chen Ji spoke, his voice crisp and decisive. The eye clearly hesitated for a moment, then satisfaction appeared in the golden vertical pupil—it believed it had caught the final soft spot of this chess piece. But what it did not see was Chen Ji's hand hidden in his sleeve, gently curling, as a tiny talisman silently took shape between his fingertips. 'I can tell you the location of the first page.' He raised his head, yet within the depths of his eyes burned a cold,幽光 flame, 'But I have one condition—I must witness the prophecy being altered first.'

The Heavenly Dao's eye fell silent for a moment, then emitted a low, guttural laugh. 'You think you have room to negotiate?' Its tone carried an imperious generosity, 'Very well, showing you some good faith won't harm me.' The golden vertical pupil abruptly expanded, countless rays of light projecting from within, weaving through the void to create a blurred image—the Chapter Seven Hundred prophecy inscription slowly fading, replaced by a new annotation: Chapter Seven Hundred, Transformation. Chen Ji stared fixedly at those two words, his pupils rapidly calculating beneath the surface. 'Transformation...' he murmured, a chill spreading through his heart. Transformation wasn't survival—it was another form of death and rebirth.

choices.text: Completely refuse, never surrender the trump cards
choices.description: Even if threatened by Heavenly Dao, will not give up a single page of Tianji Record information, holding firm to the final leverage
choices.visible_cost: Immediately face Heavenly Dao's trial-level suppression
choices.visible_reward: Building an 'unbribable' persona before Heavenly Mandate carries profound significance.
choices.risk_hint: This could lead to severe Heavenly Fate depletion, or even cause immediate severe injury.

text.content: "Two words, 'I won't hand it over,' spilled from Chen Ji's mouth, as crisp as a blade slicing through jade. The amusement in that golden giant pupil froze instantly, the vertical pupil narrowing into a dangerous thin line. The temperature in the void plummeted, a suffocating pressure crushing down like substantial matter. Chen Ji felt every bone in his body groaning, yet he stood straight, even a hint of calm smile hanging at the corner of his lips. 'Listen carefully—' he confronted that oppressive might, speaking word by word, 'The Tianji Record is not your bestowed favor; it's an inheritance my Chen ancestors traded their lives for. Even if I die, I will never make such a transaction.'"

choices.text: Turning the tables: "Aren't you also begging me?"
choices.description: Pointing out that Heavenly Mandate truly desires the Tianji Record Fragment, proving it needs him alive, is itself the greatest vulnerability.
choices.visible_cost: Completely infuriating Heavenly Mandate, losing all possibility of reconciliation.
choices.visible_reward: For the first time overwhelming Heavenly Mandate in momentum, seizing control of the dialogue.
choices.risk_hint: A single misstep in these words would become Heavenly Mandate's justification for total annihilation.

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly burst into laughter. Not a cold laugh, not a bitter laugh, but genuine laughter from the depths of his heart, carrying three parts of carefree delight. 'You're begging me.' He raised his head, gazing directly into that golden giant pupil. 'If you truly possessed the power to erase me, why negotiate with me? You could simply act. The reason you offered a price is because you need me—need me to willingly surrender the Tianji Record, not have it forcibly taken.' He stepped forward. 'What does this indicate? It means once the host of the Tianji Record Fragment dies or resists, the fragment will automatically flee into the void, forever beyond your reach. Correct?' An eerie silence descended through the void. That golden vertical pupil trembled violently for an instant—a moment where the Eye of Heavenly Mandate, across billions of years, had for the first time revealed what could only be called 'vacillation' before a mere mortal.

The golden pupil's tremor lasted only a moment before restoring its ancient, unchanging coldness. But Chen Ji had captured that fleeting shift—this was precisely what he wanted. What a chess master fears most isn't losing, but discovering their opponent isn't taking the game seriously. Now he understood: the Eye of Heavenly Mandate wasn't omniscient. It too needed to scheme, to strategize, and had rules it couldn't directly bypass. 'Interesting.' he murmured. 'So even you have moments of needing to ask for help.'

The void's eye gradually closed. Not vanishing, but shutting—like an ancient stone statue lowering its eyelids. In the darkness, only the three sacred flames on the altar still burned, black, white, and gray light stretching Chen Ji's shadow to extreme length. At this moment, an elderly and familiar voice emerged from the Tianji Record Fragment over his chest: 'It's gone. At least for today, it won't trouble you further.' It was Mo Xiansheng. Chen Ji's heart tightened. As he was about to speak, Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out again, carrying an unusual gravity: 'But the final words it spoke before leaving, did you hear them?'

Chen Ji had indeed heard those words. They pierced his heart like a thin needle, embedding themselves in the softest part of his being. 'The death you think is false is merely a performance I've permitted.' He recalled his plan—a staged death to deceive heaven, quietly gathering strength, waiting for the right moment to act. That plan he had shared with no one, not even Mo Xiansheng. Yet the Eye of Heavenly Mandate spoke with such certainty, as if from the moment he devised that strategy, it had already been seated across the chessboard, seeing each move with perfect clarity. 'How did it know?' Chen Ji's voice was hoarse. 'Unless...' He didn't finish, but the answer was almost self-evident—unless from the very beginning, what he believed to be 'secret machinations' had already been observed by a higher-dimensional existence, like an audience watching a play, observing him编织着命运的棋局。

The altar slowly descended, its three sacred flames merging into a single radiant beam that enveloped Chen Ji. A warm, replenishing energy surged through his body, reminiscent of a parched riverbed finally receiving an upstream flood. 'Trial complete.' Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out again. 'You have passed the first trial—demonstrating neither servility nor surrender in the face of fate, refusing to succumb to threats or enticements. This spirit is precisely what the Tianji Record values most.' Chen Ji felt his cultivation subtly elevate within that sacred flame. The initial barrier of Foundation Building showed its first subtle crack. 'Is this merely the first trial?' he murmured. 'Volume One's objective,' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried an enigmatic depth, 'is to gather seven fragments of the Tianji Record. And this, is merely the beginning.'

The sacred flames dissipated, and the altar completely submerged into the void. Chen Ji suddenly found himself standing at the exit of the Tianji Pavilion ruins, facing a stone door radiating soft light. The token in his hand had already dimmed, its surface runes completely vanished, as if it had never existed. He lowered his gaze to his right hand—moments ago, his cultivation had broken through from Foundation Building initial stage to middle stage, spiritual energy flow increasing by nearly half. 'Indeed, trials of life and death most effectively unlock potential.' he murmured to himself, a complex smile playing at the corners of his mouth. This trial, he had passed. But the lingering implications of the Eye of Heavenly Mandate's final words continued to echo in his heart, refusing to dissipate.

Chen Ji pushed open the stone door, and sunlight poured in, illuminating his stern features. The sky beyond the ruins remained unchanged, the mountains and rivers as they had always been, yet his mindset had transformed completely. He was no longer a blind chess piece stumbling through darkness—he knew an eye watched from above, every step potentially preordained. Yet precisely because of this, he saw the boundaries of the chessboard for the first time. 'Eye of Heavenly Mandate...' He raised his head toward the crystal-clear heavens, unprecedented light burning in his eyes. 'You think I am on your chessboard, but you forget—I too wish to witness what expression you wear when the chess player himself becomes a mere piece.' His fingers tightened into a fist within his sleeve. A grander game of strategy was unfolding beneath his feet.
